## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (68%)** · Unreliable input · Careful review
Reliability flag raised [F6]; Normal is also in the 90% set [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 68%, Normal 32% | Benign leads; Normal plausible |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.58 / 8th percentile, flagged | Input suspect |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Models agree |
| Similar cases | 0 of 5 Benign; all Normal [F5] | Neighbors favor Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 3, 8, 9) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Weak
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 1, 5, 11) · ↓ invasive · Strongest negative term, but failed spot check [F2] · Unreliable
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 0) · ↓ invasive · Near-zero contribution; score only slightly above typical · Validated
- **Mean nuclear area 49 µm²** (regions 0, 3, 10) · context · Smallest in reference set; three sampled regions only [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007); not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Image quality problems distort the scores; Normal and Benign are not separable at 90%.
- If region 3's 61 HoVer-Net neoplastic nuclei are truly atypical, the near-zero invasive probability is understated.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 3:** Decide whether the 61 HoVer-Net neoplastic nuclei are benign epithelium or atypical.
2. **Regions 1, 5, 11:** Judge lobular architecture directly; the normal-lobule score failed its spot check.
3. **Region 0:** Look for stromal infiltration, where tumor-infiltrating stroma scores highest.
